nodes.summary: An elementary integrand with `n` intervals is bounded by `n * bound`.
nodes.title: Uniform bound on an elementary integrand

nodes.summary: For a locally integrable `f : ℝ → ℝ`, for almost every `u`, the averages of `f` over intervals `[a n, b n]` converge to `f u` whenever the lengths `b n - a n > 0` tend to `0` and the distance from `u` to the midpoint of `[a n, b n]` is at most twice the length.
nodes.title: Lebesgue differentiation along shrinking off-center intervals

nodes.summary: For a Brownian motion `B`, almost surely, for every `t ≥ 0` and every initial value `X₀`, the Itô–Riemann sums `e^{-θt} X₀ + σ e^{-θt} ∑_{k < n} e^{θ t k / n} (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))` of `e^{-θt} X₀ + σ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-s)} dB_s` converge to the pathwise solution `ouPathSolution` (any real `θ`, `σ`).
nodes.title: The Itô form of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck solution

nodes.summary: The `L²` Itô integral is (almost surely equal to) an `F t`-measurable function.
nodes.title: Measurability of the $L^2$ Itô integral

nodes.summary: Itô-approximability on `[0, t]` only depends on the integrand at times in `(0, t]`.
nodes.title: Locality of approximability

nodes.summary: The delayed-average approximation of a progressive process `H` on `[0, t]`, truncated at level `M`, with `n + 1` intervals: on `(t_k, t_{k+1}]`, with `t_k = k t / (n + 1)`, it equals the average of `truncation (H ·) M` over `[t_{k-1}, t_k]` for `k ≥ 1`, and `0` for `k = 0`. For `M ≤ 0` the truncation, and hence the approximation, is `0`.
nodes.title: Delayed-average approximation of a progressive process

nodes.summary: The partition intervals of an elementary integrand are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.title: Partition intervals of an elementary integrand are disjoint

nodes.summary: An elementary integrand for a filtration `F` indexed by `ℝ≥0`: partition times `time 0 ≤ ⋯ ≤ time n` and coefficients `coeff i`, bounded by `bound` and measurable with respect to `F (time i)`, representing the process `∑ i, coeff i 1_{(time i, time (i + 1)]}`. Equal consecutive times are allowed (the corresponding interval is empty).
nodes.title: Elementary integrand

nodes.summary: Polarized Itô isometry for elementary integrands: for a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` whose increments `B t - B s` are independent of `F s`, and two elementary integrands `H`, `K` (with possibly different partitions), `E[(∫_0^t H dB) (∫_0^t K dB)] = E ∫_0^t H_u K_u du`.
nodes.title: Polarized Itô isometry

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` whose increments `B t - B s` are independent of `F s`, `E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = ∑ i, E[ξ_i²] (t_{i+1} ∧ t - t_i ∧ t)`.
nodes.title: Itô isometry, discrete form

nodes.summary: Itô isometry for elementary integrands: for a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` whose increments `B t - B s` are independent of `F s`, `E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = E ∫_0^t H_u² du` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2.A).
nodes.title: Itô isometry

nodes.summary: The second moment of a Brownian increment: `E[(B v - B r)²] = v - r` for `r ≤ v`.
nodes.title: Second moment of a Brownian increment

nodes.summary: The time integral of the squared elementary integrand, path by path: `∫_0^t H_u² du = ∑ i, ξ_i² (t_{i+1} ∧ t - t_i ∧ t)`.
nodes.title: Time integral of a squared elementary integrand

nodes.summary: The squared `L²(P ⊗ du)` distance between two Itô-approximable integrands is the squared `L²(P)` distance between their Itô integrals.
nodes.title: Itô isometry for Itô-approximable integrands

nodes.summary: `integrandDist` of two elementary integrands is the squared `L²(P)` distance of their Itô integrals.
nodes.title: Itô isometry for elementary integrands

nodes.summary: The integrand distance on `(0, t]` is the square of the `L²` seminorm on `Ω × (0, t]`.
nodes.title: Integrand distance as a squared $L^2$ seminorm

nodes.summary: Pointwise `|x - y|² ≤ 2 |x - z|² + 2 |y - z|²`, integrated: a quasi-triangle inequality for `integrandDist` between jointly measurable processes.
nodes.title: Quasi-triangle inequality for the integrand distance

nodes.summary: The `L²(P ⊗ du)` distance between two elementary integrands is finite.
nodes.title: Finite distance between elementary integrands

nodes.summary: `integrandDist P X Y t` only depends on `X` and `Y` at times in `(0, t]`.
nodes.title: Integrand distance depends only on times in (0, t)

nodes.summary: The squared `L²(P ⊗ du)` distance on `(0, t] × Ω` between two processes, in `ℝ≥0∞`: `∫⁻ ω, ∫⁻ u in (0, t], |H u ω - K u ω|² du dP`.
nodes.title: Squared $L^2$ distance between integrands

nodes.summary: A progressive integrand `H` with `E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞` is the `L²(P ⊗ du)`-limit on `(0, t] × Ω` of elementary integrands (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Lemma 3.2.4 and Proposition 3.2.6).
nodes.title: Density of elementary integrands

nodes.summary: An elementary integrand is Itô-approximable on every `[0, t]` (by itself).
nodes.title: Elementary integrands are Itô-approximable

nodes.summary: A process `H` is Itô-approximable on `[0, t]` for the filtration `F` if it is jointly measurable on `(0, t] × Ω` and is the `L²(P ⊗ du)`-limit on `(0, t] × Ω` of elementary integrands. Neither condition involves the values of `H` at time `0` or after `t`.
nodes.title: Itô-approximable process

nodes.summary: The Itô integral `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` as a real process: an `F t`-strongly measurable version of `itoIntegralL2 P F B H t` when one exists (which is the case under the hypotheses of the theorems below), and a representative of `itoIntegralL2 P F B H t` otherwise.
nodes.title: Itô integral process

nodes.summary: The Itô integral is additive in the integrand: for `F`-progressive integrands `H₁, H₂` with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the integral of the sum is almost surely the sum of the integrals. Together with homogeneity and the difference isometry this pins down the integral on the whole `L²` space of progressive integrands. Only the pre-Brownian finite-dimensional laws are used; path continuity is not required.
nodes.title: Linearity (additivity)

nodes.summary: The Itô integral is additive in the integrand: for `F`-progressive integrands `H₁, H₂` with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the integral of the sum is almost surely the sum of the integrals. Together with homogeneity and the difference isometry this pins down the integral on the whole `L²` space of progressive integrands.
nodes.title: Linearity (additivity)

nodes.summary: The Itô integral process is almost surely equal to `itoIntegralL2` at each time.
nodes.title: Itô integral process is a version of the $L^2$ integral

nodes.summary: The Itô integral admits a modification with continuous paths: there is a process `J` with continuous paths such that `J t = ∫_0^t H dB` almost surely for each `t` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2). `ProbabilityTheory.itoIntegral` chooses its version separately at each time, so it is only determined up to a null set that may depend on `t`; the statement therefore asks for a modification rather than for a process…
nodes.title: Continuous modification

nodes.summary: For a Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and a deterministic `C¹` integrand `g`, the Itô integral is `∫_0^t g dB = g t B t - g 0 B 0 - ∫_0^t g'(u) B u du` almost surely (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.3; the right side is a pathwise Riemann integral).
nodes.title: Wiener's integration by parts

nodes.summary: For `a ≤ b` and a bounded `F a`-measurable `ξ`, the Itô integral of `ξ 1_{(a, b]}` against a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past is `ξ (B (b ∧ t) - B (a ∧ t))` almost surely (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2.A).
nodes.title: Elementary integrands

nodes.summary: For two `F`-progressive integrands with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the difference of the integrals is square-integrable and `E[(∫ H₁ dB - ∫ H₂ dB)²] = E ∫ (H₁ - H₂)² du`. With linearity this is the two-integrand isometry that, together with the elementary-integrand formula, determines the construction on the whole `L²` space. Only the pre-Brownian finite-dimensional laws are used; path continuity is not required.
nodes.title: Difference isometry

nodes.summary: For two `F`-progressive integrands with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the difference of the integrals is square-integrable and `E[(∫ H₁ dB - ∫ H₂ dB)²] = E ∫ (H₁ - H₂)² du`. With linearity this is the two-integrand isometry that, together with the elementary-integrand formula, determines the construction on the whole `L²` space.
nodes.title: Difference isometry

nodes.summary: The Itô integral at time `t` only depends on the integrand at times in `(0, t]`.
nodes.title: Locality of the Itô integral

nodes.summary: The Itô integral `∫_0^t H dB` as an element of `L²(P)`: the `L²` limit of the elementary Itô integrals of an approximating sequence of elementary integrands when `H` is Itô-approximable on `[0, t]`, and `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: Itô integral as an element of $L^2$

nodes.summary: The elementary Itô integral of `riemann F g t n` at time `t` is the Itô–Riemann sum `∑_{k < n} g (t k / n) (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))`.
nodes.title: Itô integral of a Riemann step approximation

nodes.summary: The Itô integral of `ξ 1_{(a, b]}` is `ξ (B (b ∧ t) - B (a ∧ t))` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2.A); this holds for every process `B` and every `ω`, by definition.
nodes.title: Elementary integrands

nodes.summary: The Itô integral is homogeneous in the integrand for a pre-Brownian integrator; path continuity is not required.
nodes.title: Linearity (homogeneity)

nodes.summary: The Itô integral is homogeneous in the integrand.
nodes.title: Linearity (homogeneity)

nodes.summary: On an elementary integrand, the Itô integral agrees almost surely with the elementary Itô integral.
nodes.title: Itô integral agrees with the elementary integral on elementary integrands

nodes.summary: The elementary Itô integral vanishes at time `0`.
nodes.title: Elementary Itô integral vanishes at time zero

nodes.summary: The Itô integral of an elementary integrand against a process `B`: `t ↦ ∑ i, coeff i (B (time (i + 1) ∧ t) - B (time i ∧ t))`.
nodes.title: Itô integral of an elementary integrand

nodes.summary: For a Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past, any initial value `X₀` and any real `θ`, `σ`, the Itô form `e^{-θt} X₀ + σ e^{-θt} ∫_0^t e^{θs} dB_s = e^{-θt} X₀ + σ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-s)} dB_s` of the solution of `dX = -θ X dt + σ dB` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6) agrees almost surely with the pathwise solution `ouPathSolution`, which solves `X t = X₀ - θ ∫_0^t X + σ (B t - B 0)`…
nodes.title: The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck solution in Itô form

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and an `F`-progressive integrand `H` with `E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞`, `E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = E ∫_0^t H_u² du` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2).
nodes.title: Itô isometry for progressive integrands

nodes.summary: Itô isometry for the `L²` Itô integral, in `ℝ≥0∞` form: for a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and an integrand `H` that is Itô-approximable on `[0, t]`, `E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = E ∫_0^t H_u² du` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2).
nodes.title: Itô isometry

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and an integrand `H` that is Itô-approximable on every `[0, t]`, the Itô integral `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` is an `F`-martingale (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Proposition 3.2.10).
nodes.title: Martingale property of the Itô integral

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and an `F`-progressive integrand `H` with `E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞` for every `t`, the Itô integral `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` is an `F`-martingale (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Proposition 3.2.10).
nodes.title: Martingale property for progressive integrands

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` whose increments `B t - B s` are independent of `F s`, the elementary Itô integral `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` is an `F`-martingale.
nodes.title: Martingale property

nodes.summary: For a progressive `H` and `b ≤ T`, the average of `u ↦ H u ω` over `[a, b]` is `F T`-measurable in `ω`.
nodes.title: Measurability of time averages of a progressive process

nodes.summary: Restricting a jointly measurable process to the times `(0, t]` keeps it jointly measurable.
nodes.title: Restriction to (0, t) preserves joint measurability

nodes.summary: A progressive process is jointly measurable in `(u, ω)` (reading `u : ℝ` through `Real.toNNReal`).
nodes.title: Progressive processes are jointly measurable

nodes.summary: An elementary integrand is jointly measurable in `(u, ω)` (reading `u : ℝ` through `Real.toNNReal`).
nodes.title: Elementary integrands are jointly measurable

nodes.summary: The elementary Itô integral against a pre-Brownian motion is square integrable.
nodes.title: Square integrability of the elementary Itô integral

nodes.summary: The Itô integral at each time is square integrable: it is a version of the element `itoIntegralL2 P F B H t` of `L²(P)` (which is `0` when `H` is not Itô-approximable).
nodes.title: Square integrability of the Itô integral

nodes.summary: The pathwise Ornstein–Uhlenbeck solution in integration-by-parts form: with `g u = e^{θu}`, `ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w t = e^{-θt} x₀ + σ e^{-θt} (g t w t - g 0 w 0 - ∫_0^t g'(u) w u du)`, for any path `w` and any real `θ`, `σ`, `x₀`, `t`.
nodes.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck path solution by integration by parts

nodes.summary: The process `H` with its values at times outside `(0, t]` set to `0`. Only the values at times in `(0, t]` enter the Itô integral at time `t`.
nodes.title: Restriction of a process to the time interval (0, t)

nodes.summary: The left-point step approximation `∑_{k < n} g (t k / n) 1_{(t k / n, t (k + 1) / n]}` of a deterministic `g` on the uniform partition of `[0, t]` into `n` cells, as an elementary integrand for any filtration `F` (deterministic coefficients are measurable for every σ-algebra).
nodes.title: Left-point step approximation of a deterministic integrand

nodes.summary: The elementary integrand `ξ 1_{(a, b]}` for `a ≤ b` and an `F a`-measurable `ξ` bounded by `C`.
nodes.title: Single-step elementary integrand

nodes.summary: For a progressive `H` and a finite measure `P`, the delayed-average approximations of the truncation of `H` at level `M` converge to it in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω` as the mesh `t / (n + 1)` tends to `0` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, proof of Lemma 3.2.4(b)).
nodes.title: Convergence of the delayed averages

nodes.summary: The left-point approximations of a continuous deterministic `g` converge to `g` in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω`.
nodes.title: $L^2$ convergence of left-point approximations of a continuous function

nodes.summary: For a jointly measurable `H` with `E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞`, the truncations of `H` at levels `M → ∞` converge to `H` in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, proof of Lemma 3.2.4(c)).
nodes.title: Truncation

nodes.summary: Along every continuous path of `B`, the elementary Itô integrals at time `t` of the left-point approximations of `g` converge to Wiener's integration-by-parts expression `g t B t - g 0 B 0 - ∫_0^t g'(u) B u du`.
nodes.title: Itô–Riemann sums of a deterministic `C¹` integrand

nodes.summary: For a `C¹` function `g`, a continuous path `w` and `t ≥ 0`, the left-point sums `∑_{k < n} g (t k / n) (w (t (k + 1) / n) - w (t k / n))` converge, as `n → ∞`, to `g t w t - g 0 w 0 - ∫_0^t g' w`.
nodes.title: Riemann–Stieltjes integration by parts, uniform partitions

nodes.summary: For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past, an `H` jointly measurable on `(0, t] × Ω`, and *any* sequence of elementary integrands `Kn` converging to `H` in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω`, the elementary Itô integrals of `Kn` converge in `L²(P)` to `itoIntegralL2 P F B H t`.
nodes.title: The Itô integral is well defined

nodes.summary: A function as an element of `L²(P)`, or `0` if it is not square integrable.
nodes.title: Function as an element of $L^2$

nodes.summary: On its `i`-th interval, an elementary integrand equals its `i`-th coefficient.
nodes.title: Elementary integrand on a partition interval

nodes.summary: The process of `single a b hab ξ hξ C hξC` is `u ↦ ξ 1_{(a, b]}(u)`.
nodes.title: Process of a single-step elementary integrand

nodes.summary: The elementary integrand as a process: `u ↦ ∑ i, coeff i 1_{(time i, time (i + 1)]}(u)`.
nodes.title: Elementary integrand as a process

nodes.summary: Truncating a progressive process at level `M` (Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.truncation`, which keeps the values in `(-M, M]` and sets the others to `0`) gives a progressive process.
nodes.title: Truncation of a progressive process is progressive

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
